claims.text: Idempotency: sending the same confirmed promotion twice (a double submit or a retry) saves one rule and one case-log entry. The second request carries the stale expected log position and is refused. New test: test_resending_the_same_confirmed_promotion_saves_one_rule.

claims.text: Partial failure and rollback: if the case log refuses the promotion entry, the firm rules file is put back as it was (existing test). A malformed firm rules file refuses both the preview and the promotion, and leaves the file's bytes and the case log unchanged (new test). A rules file changed by another case after the preview is read as it now stands: the other rule is kept and the new one takes a fresh id (new test).

Data and PII: firm_rules.yaml holds counterparty names and reasons. It is written by atomic rename and is readable by its owner only (no group or other bits; new test: test_the_firm_rules_file_is_written_readable_by_its_owner_only). The case-log entry carries neither the pattern nor the reason (existing test). The migration is additive: a new file at the case root, and a missing file means no rules.

Test defect fixed: in test_the_page_shows_the_promote_form_and_the_preview_escaped, the page-content checks sat inside the assert's message expression (`assert status == 200, raw and b'...' in raw`), so they never ran. They are now a separate assert, and they pass.

Observability: the promotion is a case-log event (firm_rule_promotion) with the rule id, direction, category, source override, matched and applies counts, name, OS user, time and the rules file's sha256. It is tested in test_promoting_saves_the_rule_logs_it_and_later_cases_apply_it. Remote alerting is not applicable: the design has none (Observability). A failure surfaces as a refusal with a non-zero status.
Configured runner tiers pass: ruff, compileall over src, the full suite and the contracts tier.

notes:
Gaps for the owner (design-level; not built here):
(1) Concurrency across cases: firm_rules.yaml is shared by every case, but promote() holds only the open case's lock. Its byte comparison just before the write (now != before) narrows the window but leaves a TOCTOU gap: two cases promoting at the same instant can lose one rule. The fix needs a lock beside firm_rules.yaml, like the checkpoint file's lock in R53, which is a design decision.
(2) The firm rules file has no change log of its own. The promotion is recorded only in the case it came from, and a hand edit or deletion of a rule leaves no trace beyond the file's hash in later evidence.
(3) The preview list is unbounded in the HTML page. A broad pattern on a 10,000-line case renders every match. R52's paging of lines does not yet cover the preview.
(4) The tests are marked contracts, and none is named p<n>. If R20/R21 promotion is meant to prove P16 (a protected line never takes a firm rule), an invariants-marked p16 test over promotion would make that visible to the runner.
(5) The changes are left uncommitted in the worktree, so the producer or verifier can review them.
